parsed.why: Documented state-targeted persecution: police torture, forced anal exams, witch-hunt committees, website blocking, and a trans activist abducted and mutilated. Same-sex criminalisation plus severe official hostility makes outing catastrophic.

Gender identity protected in human-rights and hate-crime law, with provincial recourse and identity-based prison placement. Rising hate crime and provincial rollbacks are concerning but do not create visitor-facing border, facility, or custody exposure.

No same-sex criminalisation, but no broad anti-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition, conservative hostility, police harassment of LGBTQ visibility, and weak trans-specific recourse. Outing risks major social and official friction.

No criminalisation, but documented trans-specific discrimination, trans women fleeing violence, police often ignoring anti-LGBT violence, no broad anti-discrimination law, and official hostility such as banning a trans commemoration.

No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or gender identity, no facility or entry restrictions, and open border. But gender identity lacks hate-crime protection, no legal gender recognition, and enforcement data are thin.
